title: Baby Sensory: Lights and Sound
strapline: Soft light, gentle sound, and cause-and-effect a baby can make happen.
intent: Gentle light and sound give babies rich sensory experiences to explore at their own pace.
Discovering that shaking or pressing makes something happen builds early cause-and-effect.
Reaching for and grasping light-up and sound toys develops coordination.
A calm sensory space supports regulation and comfort for unsettled babies.
Sharing the wonder with an adult turns exploration into connection and talk.
implementation: Offer safe light-up toys, fibre-optics and soft-sound makers in a calm, low-lit corner.
Follow the baby's lead — let them reach, mouth, shake and pause without hurrying.
Show cause and effect gently: "you shook it and it lit up!".
Keep sounds soft and varied — bells, rain-makers, crinkle, gentle music.
Use the space for calming as well as exploring, reading the baby's cues.
Narrate simply and warmly what the baby sees, hears and does.
key_questions: What happened when you shook it?
Do you like this gentle sound?
Shall we make it happen again?

impact.text: Babies explore light, colour and sound with their whole bodies and senses.
Babies discover that their action makes something happen.
Babies reach, grasp and explore objects with growing control.
Babies settle and regulate with responsive care in a calm space.
Babies respond to sound and music with stilling, movement and delight.

enhancements: Safe light-up toys, fibre-optic strands and a projector for gentle colour.
Soft-sound makers: bells, rain-makers, crinkle and shakers.
A calm, low-lit corner with cushions and a blackout option.
Reflective and translucent materials to catch the light.
A treasure basket of light- and sound-making natural objects.
Time and permission to explore or to calm, led by the baby.

playing_exploring: Babies explore light and sound freely, at their own pace and in their own way.
active_learning: Babies repeat an action to make the light or sound happen again.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to connect their own movement to the effect it creates.
